about.text: A spreadable cheese from the mountains of Abruzzo, made chiefly around Castel del Monte, also called cacio or pecorino marcetto. Cheese flies (Piophila casei) lay eggs in cracks in a ripening raw-milk pecorino. Their larvae break down the proteins and turn the paste into a very sharp cream, which is packed into glass or terracotta jars.

how.label: let larvae soften
how.text: Pecorino wheels that are still moist with whey or have cracked rinds are colonised by cheese-fly larvae, whose activity breaks down the proteins until the whole wheel turns creamy and very piquant. The paste is then scraped out and kept refrigerated in terracotta or glass jars as a spreadable cream.
